title: LRU Cache Implementation
description: Implement an LRU cache using a doubly-linked list and hash map for O(1) get and put operations.

segments.text: Time to implement the LRU cache. The key insight: we need O(1) get and O(1) put. That means a hash map for fast lookup combined with a doubly-linked list for fast ordering. Let's build it.
Two data structures working together. The HashMap maps keys to linked list nodes. The doubly-linked list maintains access order, most recent at the head, least recent at the tail.
The Node class holds key, value, prev pointer, and next pointer. We use sentinel head and tail nodes to eliminate null checks at boundaries. Every real node sits between the sentinels.

Get operation: look up the key in the hash map. If found, move the node to the head of the list, it was just accessed, then return the value. If not found, return negative one. Both operations are O(1).

Put operation: if the key exists, update its value and move to head. If it is new, create a node, add to head, insert into the map. If capacity is exceeded, remove the tail node and delete its key from the map.

segments.thought_prompt: Why do we store the key inside the Node, when the HashMap already maps key to node?

segments.text: Because when we evict the tail node, we need to remove it from the HashMap too. We have the node but need its key to delete the map entry. Without the key stored in the node, we cannot do this in O(1).
Two helper methods: addToHead inserts a node right after the sentinel head. removeNode detaches a node by updating its neighbors' pointers. Moving to head is just removeNode followed by addToHead.

In Java, use a LinkedHashMap with accessOrder set to true and override removeEldestEntry. That gives you LRU in three lines. But in an interview, implement it from scratch to show you understand the internals.
In Python, collections.OrderedDict gives you move_to_end and popitem. But again, building it manually with a dict and custom doubly-linked list is what interviewers want to see.

segments.thought_prompt: What happens if two threads call get and put simultaneously on the same key? What could go wrong?

segments.text: Race conditions. The list pointers could become corrupted. We will solve that in the next lesson on thread safety. For now, you have a complete single-threaded LRU cache with O(1) get and put. That is a classic interview problem, solved.
